title: screamingface-engine chart values
description: Validated at `helm lint`/`helm install` time. WHY this file exists: a chart's values are an API, and without a schema they are an UNTYPED one — `runner.backend` was a free-form string that only screamingface_engine.config.Settings validated, at container startup, i.e. after a successful deploy reported success. Everything encoded here fails before anything is applied to a cluster.

logLevel.description: The level the screamingface_engine logger tree runs at (OME-942), rendered to BOTH the App and the runner pool as URL4_CLOUD_LOG_LEVEL. Constrained to the names logging.Logger.setLevel resolves: an unknown name raises inside the handler install at boot, so the pod crashloops with a traceback naming the logging module rather than the values file.

natsUrl.description: Empty is legal: the natsUrl helper then derives it from nats.fullnameOverride, or fails the render.

jobDeadlineS.description: Job activeDeadlineSeconds. INVARIANT: the 16h ceiling is spec §3.

orphanGraceS.description: Seconds a run may keep going with no WebSocket subscriber before the App stops it (OME-890); 0 disables the reaper. INVARIANT: the audience count is in-process, so replicaCount must stay 1 while this is non-zero — a second replica would answer "nobody is listening" for runs another replica is streaming. Keep it above uvicorn's WS ping window (~40s), which is what closes a partitioned client's socket in the first place.

unclaimedRunWarnS.description: Seconds a queued run may wait with no frame before its attached client gets one generic WARN notice; 0 disables it. Advisory only — the run is never failed or stopped. Keep it well above a healthy claim latency (seconds) so it fires only on a saturated or absent runner pool. INVARIANT: assumes replicaCount 1 — only the replica that scheduled a run warns, so with more than one App replica a client whose WebSocket lands on another replica is silently never warned.

runnerIoConcurrency.description: Per-run downstream in-flight budget written onto every Runner Job as URL4_CLOUD_IO_CONCURRENCY (OME-908). 4 matches the gateway's per-provider admission ceiling so a run saturates its provider without piling a backlog behind it; 32 restores the pre-OME-908 width. Local mode ignores this value (its runs share the process fair-share gate).

runQueueReplicas.description: The queue stream's replica count (OME-1088), rendered to both the App and the worker pool — they declare the same singleton stream and ensure_stream refuses a divergent declaration, so a one-sided value is a startup failure for whichever half declares second. Defaults to 1 because this chart bundles a SINGLE-NODE NATS subchart, and a single-node broker refuses replicas > 1 outright (ServerError 10074). Raise it only against a real NATS cluster.

runQueueBucketCount.description: How many bucket subjects the run queue is split into for per-caller fairness (OME-1091), rendered to both the App and the worker pool. The App publishes into one bucket and the worker polls them all, so a one-sided value is NOT a startup failure — the run is accepted, lands in a bucket nobody polls, and expires silently. Zero is the modulus of the bucket hash, so it is refused here before any template renders.

aigatewayModel.description: Overrides the default model route declared in the Runner image's url4.toml. Empty uses the image default; must name a model url4.toml declares.

config.$comment: `port` was removed deliberately: the App serves on a hardcoded 9108 (cli.py) and reads no port from its environment, so the value only ever moved the containerPort away from the listening port — a render that lint and install both accepted while the probes and the Service targetPort pointed at nothing. additionalProperties:false now rejects it at install time instead.

events.description: The shared events stream (`url4-events`, uniform executor PRD 01 §4). Rendered to BOTH the App and the runner pool — both halves apply their OWN configured limits to the live stream at startup (ensure_events_stream(..., update=True)); every field below is MUTABLE, so a one-sided value is NOT a startup failure but silently flips the shared stream's limits back and forth on every rollout. Only an IMMUTABLE field (storage, retention — neither configurable here) failing to match fails startup. Both halves must render from the SAME values for that reason.

maxBytes.description: Must fit the broker's JetStream file store, or startup fails naming `events.maxBytes` (erd.md §5 EV-D9). Default 1 GiB. When the store is full, JetStream drops the OLDEST frames of whichever subject they belong to (ans:Q11); `screamingface_engine_events_store_utilization_ratio` is the alert signal to raise this from.

maxMsgsPerSubject.description: One run's frame retention bound per SUBJECT, regardless of the store's overall use. Default 20000 — 10x the measured p99 frame count headroom (PRD 01 §6). A rollover keeps the terminal frame: a purge always keeps the last message.

maxAgeS.description: Storage backstop: a subject nobody ever purges (a crashed runner, EV-D13) clears itself after this many seconds — no sweep is needed. Default 86400 (24h).

replicas.description: Same posture as `config.runQueueReplicas`: this chart bundles a SINGLE-NODE NATS subchart, which refuses `replicas > 1` outright (ServerError 10074). Raise it only against a real NATS cluster (OME-1093).

backend.description: Mirrors screamingface_engine.config.RunnerBackend. `queue` deploys the App onto the durable run queue + worker pool; `none` deploys an App that cannot schedule and answers 503 to every run.

repository.description: Empty derives `<image.repository>-benchmark`; override when the benchmark image uses another repository.

tag.description: Empty uses the control-plane image's resolved tag; override only for a staged rollout.

runnerPool.description: The fixed worker pool (OME-1092): a Deployment of `replicas` pods, each running `screamingface-engine worker` with `workerSlots` run slots. Declared concurrency is `replicas × workerSlots`.

workerSlots.description: Run slots per worker pod. MUST match `run_queue_worker_slots`. One slot is one supervised child process, so `replicas × workerSlots` is what bounds fleet execution.

warmChildren.description: Warm children per worker pod (uniform executor PRD 03). Default 2 (sized to 4 runs in flight over 2 pods). Null leaves the app default (one per worker slot) in force. 0 spawns a child on each claim instead. The worker caps this at `workerSlots`; the render also refuses a value ABOVE `workerSlots` (see the guard in deployment-runner.yaml), so a chart operator gets a render-time error instead of a silently truncated value. Each idle warm child holds the engine and its built world (~430 MiB with the builtin benchmarks); idle children only occupy FREE slots.

maxAckPending.description: The queue's PER-CALLER allowance: applied to every bucket consumer, and a caller hashes to one bucket, so it caps one caller's unacked runs (not the fleet — that is `runQueueBucketCount × this`). Null/absent derives `replicas × workerSlots`, which hands each caller the whole fleet's width; pin it whenever `replicas > 1`. Binds at consumer creation, so changing it does not re-cap a live queue.

drainGraceS.description: Seconds a draining worker keeps its in-flight children alive after SIGTERM (`worker_drain_grace_s`).

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: INVARIANT: must stay at or above `drainGraceS` + 10s (kill grace) + 15s (terminal-publish budget) — the kubelet SIGKILLs the pod at this deadline, and a drain cut short interrupts every in-flight run. The chart enforces this with a `fail` at render time; a JSON Schema description alone enforces nothing.

perRunCharge.description: The per-slot charge: what one run may consume (the old Runner Job's numbers).

overhead.description: The worker process's own footprint, added to the per-slot charge.

warmChildCharge.description: The memory one IDLE warm child holds (the engine + its built world; ~430 MiB measured in kind, implementation-notes F7), ; each warm child adds its excess over `perRunCharge.memoryMi` (its free slot's charge, already requested) to the pod's memory request.

node.description: REMOVED (uniform executor PRD 05). Any value makes the chart fail with a message.

artifactSigning.description: Shared HMAC key for a mount result's short-lived artifact URL (OQ-3.2, contracts.md C6, uniform executor PRD 05). The App signs the 303 Location over 1 MiB and verifies it on GET /artifacts/{id}, keyed URL4_CLOUD_ARTIFACT_SIGNING_KEY.

then.description: tavily.enabled needs a key source: either bring your own Secret (existingSecret) or let the chart create one from apiKey. Enabled with neither would name a Secret that does not exist, and the Runner Pod would fail to start on an unresolvable secretKeyRef.
auth.create=false means the JWT signing secret must come from somewhere — without existingSecret the Deployment references a Secret that was never created.

cloudflareAccess.description: Envoy Gateway SecurityPolicy that re-verifies Cloudflare Access and injects X-User-Email.

then.description: An HTTPRoute with no parentRef attaches to no Gateway and silently serves nothing.

allOf.description: A JWT filter with no team domain verifies nothing, and one with no audience accepts every application in the team.

natsBox.description: Upstream defaults this to true; the chart forces it off. It is an interactive shell pod with network access to the bus and no role in the running system.

artifactStorage.description: Where over-cap results are parked between the Runner Job that writes one and the App that serves it (OME-929). 'filesystem' is single-process only; separate pods need 's3'. With garage.enabled the credentials are generated and adopted automatically.

garage.description: The bundled single-node S3-compatible store. Default-disabled: an existing endpoint can be named with artifactStorage.s3.endpointUrl instead. Needs a one-time bootstrap after install — see templates/garage.yaml.

replicaCount.description: Must be 1: two Garage processes on one metadata store corrupt it.

then.description: tracing.enabled requires tracing.endpoint. Enabled with an empty endpoint would start a runner pool that exports nothing, and that state has NO runtime symptom - the trace view is simply empty, which is indistinguishable from nobody having run anything. Refusing here is the only loud moment available. Note the credential (tracing.headers) is deliberately NOT required: an in-cluster collector needs none.

$comment: additionalProperties:false is the point of this file — it turns a stale or misspelled key (a `podDisruptionBudget` block left behind after the template was deleted, a `runner.resource` typo) into an install-time error instead of a value that is silently ignored while the operator believes it took effect. `global` is allowed because Helm injects it for subcharts.
